messages:
noah: Heads-up: onboarding CustEcho LoRA (echo-base-v1 + cust-echo-lora) into staging. After int4 quant + merge we see cents disappearing in invoice outputs (e.g. '£123.45' -> '£123'). Need a short eval pack and triage.
irene: Yikes. Share the pack path, CLI you used, and tokenizer in the manifest.
noah: Pack: s3://redwood-evals/custecho/echo_onboard/4440003210/ (invoices_smoke.json, 45 cases). CLI: `rdw-infer --model echo-base-v1+cust-echo-lora --quant int4 --input invoices_smoke.json --out out.json --batch 6`. Manifest tokenizer: hf/byte-level-1. My local used hf/byte-level-2 accidentally.
samira: Paste one failing raw output and the expected. Also run a token inspect for the problematic strings.
noah: Example: 
- prompt: "Invoice total: \u00a3123.45"
- expected: "Invoice total: \u00a3123.45"
- got: "Invoice total: \u00a3123"
Token check (quick): byte-level-1 -> ['123', '.', '45'] ; byte-level-2 -> ['123', '.', '4', '5']
leo: That split explains fragility on the int4 decode path. Small single-digit tail tokens can be dropped in some compressive kernels. Two paths: (1) enforce tokenizer_compat in manifest and rerun; (2) quick runtime guard in int4 decode that keeps single-digit tokens after '.' sticky; (3) as last resort add a small postproc canonicalizer to reinstate cents when pattern matches.
irene: I'll try manifest override first and re-run the pack. If that nails it we can add a manifest unit test.
eval-bot: Quick eval (initial): fp16 cents-preserved: 44/45, int8: 42/45, int4: 31/45. Pattern: failures cluster on tokens split like ['.', '4', '5'].
noah: Re-run with manifest override in progress. If override fixes >90% we can ship a manifest note to the customer and revert the merge until we patch runtime.
samira: I'll draft a small micro-benchmark comparing fp16/int8/int4 on these 45 cases and output exact-match + numeric MSE. Putting job in queue.
patchbot: Draft PR created: https://git.redwood/infer/decoding/PR-1542 (runtime guard low-risk) 1 adds a unit test for 10 canonical amounts.
leo: If runtime guard looks safe in canary we can flip for CustEcho traffic. Also add a short helpdesk detector that flags tokenizer mismatch at upload time.
eval-bot: Benchmark job queued. ETA ~15m. Logging to s3://redwood-evals/custecho/echo_onboard/4440003210/bench.csv
noah: Thanks all. Prioritize manifest override + bench results. Ping this thread with any hotfix we can canary before the customer dry-run next week.
